tob-10051: The first book of the Bible traces the story of humanity from creation through the great flood to the family of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Readers meet Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, and Noah, then follow the patriarchs whose descendants become the twelve tribes of Israel. In the 1611 King James wording, these are the foundational narratives of both Judaism and Christianity.
tob-13151: Bulwer-Lytton’s 1871 novel sends its narrator down a mine shaft into a subterranean world ruled by the Vril-ya, a superior race wielding a mysterious all-powerful energy called ‘vril.’ Part science fiction, part social satire, it imagined technologies and gender roles far ahead of its time. The book inspired real-world occultists who took ‘vril’ seriously.
tob-4185-78851: Book three of Goodwin’s Plutarch keeps the Moralia rolling — on garrulity, on meddlesomeness, on brotherly love, and more. Plutarch’s easy blend of tale and sermon made him the old world’s dearest moral teacher. Each piece reads like counsel from a wise old friend.
tob-4151: Claud Field’s 1910 Alchemy of Happiness melts down al-Ghazali’s soul-guide — on knowing self, knowing God, and knowing the world to come. Brief and workmanlike, it is Ghazali at his plainest. The book first bore his wisdom to English readers. A fair first taste of Islam’s inward way.
cia-0000102951: Bauxite is the ore that aluminum is made from, and this January 1985 report studies Soviet bauxite mining around Severouralsk in the Ural Mountains. It examines how much the Soviets could dig up and how the mines fed their factories. The CIA watched raw materials like this closely, since metal supplies underpinned Soviet industry and weapons production.
cia-0000107451: A January 1949 report on Turkey's interests in Syrian territory and the impact of communism there. Turkey eyed borderlands it had lost after World War I, while communists probed Syria's weakness. The document captures the layered rivalries of the early Cold War Middle East, where old empires and new ideologies collided.
cia-0000112351: An August 1987 report on several UFO sightings reported by Barbadians. Caribbean islanders watched strange lights and told the press; the story traveled far enough to reach American files. The entry is a small reminder that the unexplained is a global phenomenon — and globally filed.
cia-0000115451: Volume II of a June 1981 National Intelligence Estimate on Cuban policy toward Latin America. The full estimate ran to multiple volumes — a sign of how seriously Washington took Havana's regional ambitions. This volume carries the supporting analysis behind the headline judgments.
cia-0000118651: A February 1968 report — title carrying the archive's typo for concern — on President Thieu's fear of a coup, conditions in the Mekong Delta, and more. Saigon's leader trusted almost no one, and the Tet Offensive was raging. The document is wartime Saigon in miniature: paranoia, battlefields, and survival politics.
cia-0000119751: The Hungarian situation as of 5:00 PM on November 6, 1956 — two days into the Soviet reconquest, with fighting fading into arrests. The revolution was effectively over; the reprisals were beginning. The document marks the turn from battle reporting to the accounting of defeat.
cia-0000132651: A January 1961 study titled The Military Buildup in Cuba. The island was arming at speed — Soviet weapons, Cuban soldiers, American anxiety. Written weeks before the Bay of Pigs, the document is the buildup, measured: the fortress, rising.
cia-0000134251: A 1960 report: North Korea and Cuba establishing diplomatic relations. The pariahs, exchanging ambassadors. The document is the pact: the outcasts, united.
cia-0000136051: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting observance of plans and general conditions — the truncated title cuts off when. The field was told to watch and wait. The document is the order: the plans, observed.
cia-0000136351: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing a congratulations message received from ASCHAM — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The victory lap, in cable form. The document is the congratulation: the praise, relayed.
un-ga-res-a-69-51: Resolution A/69/51, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The fifty-first act. The designation and year align; the content awaits.
un-sc-res-1451: Security Council Resolution 1451, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1751: Security Council Resolution 1751, adopted in 2007 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
cia-0000132751: A 1961 CIA Cuba file — number 0000132751. The watch continued past the Bay of Pigs. The document is the continuation: the island, still watched.
cia-0000135751: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135751, date approximate. The circa-dated set. The document is the circa: the dating, soft.
plos-pone-0000051: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: physiological mouse brain amyloid-beta levels are not related to the phosphorylation — the truncated title cuts off of what. An Alzheimer's molecule, exonerated of one suspicion. The paper is the non-relation: the levels, unlinked.
cia-0000137451: A 1971 CIA file on a South Vietnamese Liberation Army enemy proselyting office's handling of something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The archive's spelling says proselyting. The entry is the handling: the office, reported — through a typo.
cia-0000139451: A 1988 CIA Project Sun Streak file — number 0000139451. The psychic-spying program, another folder. The entry is the folder: the program, documented.
un-sc-res-351: Security Council Resolution 351, adopted in 1974 — aligned. The mid-seventies Council at work. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d51: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, October 21, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 51. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d151: The president's personal representative Hurley to the President — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 151. The envoy reported home. The cable is the envoy's: Hurley, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d251: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 251, closing the batch. The editors' bridge. The note is the close: the batch, complete.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d351: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the president's secretary — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 351. The insider answered the staff. The memo is the answer: Hopkins, to Early.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d451: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 6, 1943 — Document 451. The next day, the planners returned. The minutes are the return: the chiefs, conferring.
the-winds-of-the-world-pg6751: Talbot Mundy — the master of Indian adventure — sets this novel in the Northwest Frontier during the Great War. British officers, native princes, and German agents collide in a tale of loyalty tested by intrigue. Mundy's deep knowledge of India gives the excitement an authentic, exotic flavor.
arxiv-2605-09351: Some merging black holes spin fast — and gas-rich galactic centers could explain why. Imre Bartos and Zoltán Haiman identify a high-spin subpopulation in binary black hole mergers consistent with AGN accretion. The 2026 paper links gravitational-wave populations to their cosmic nurseries.
arxiv-2605-09551: VP and VNP are algebraic complexity's P and NP; min-plus semirings change the arithmetic underneath. Balagopal Komarath, Harshil Mittal, and Jayalal Sarma study algebraic branching programs over min-plus semirings. The 2026 paper is algebraic complexity theory in tropical territory.
arxiv-2605-09751: What if a language model had no trainable embedding table at all — just fixed minimal binary token codes? Andrey Bochkov explores whether learning is possible from them anyway. The 2026 paper boldly questions one of the field's most sacred cows ever.
plos-pone-0003451: Stem-cell biologists found mice and humans build different scaffolds in this 2008 paper. Comparing gene-expression data, they discovered that human embryonic stem cells and mouse embryonic stem cells switch on different keratin filament proteins, the structural threads of cells. The contrast warns researchers that mouse stem-cell results do not always translate directly to human biology.
plos-pone-0003551: Geneticists stress-tested their gap-filling tools in this 2008 comparison. When genotype data are missing, researchers impute, or guess, the absent variants, and the team measured how accurate different imputation methods really are. The head-to-head comparison guides gene-hunters toward methods that hold up when data run thin.
plos-pone-0003651: In 2008, Lucchetta, Vincent, and Ismagilov tested how perfect an embryo map must be. The Bicoid protein forms a gradient that tells a fly embryo head from tail, but the team showed the gradient need not be exact during cycles 11 to 13 for the body plan to come out right. Precision, it turns out, can wait.
plos-pone-0003751: In 2008, Leal, Flores, and García-Cortés weighed blood tests for a childhood stomach bug. Their meta-analysis compared antibody-based tests for Helicobacter pylori infection in children. The pooled verdict guides which test to trust when young patients need answers.
plos-pone-0003851: A 2008 stroke study found late help still helps. Delayed postconditioning, briefly interrupting blood flow after it returns, protected rat brains from focal ischemic injury. The result extends the treatment window for stroke, suggesting even late intervention can limit brain damage.
plos-pone-0003951: In 2008, Yu, Macdonald, and Liu repurposed an old worm drug against cancer. Pyrvinium pamoate hit the unfolded protein response under low sugar, and pairing it with other drugs boosted its tumor killing. The anthelminthic's second career targets cancer's metabolic stress.
plos-pone-0004051: In 2008, Mendiola, Barriuso, and Redondo hunted vessel genes that predict ovarian cancer fate. An angiogenesis-related gene expression profile carried independent prognostic value for patients. The gene signature flagged which advanced ovarian carcinomas would fare worst. The profile offers doctors a molecular crystal ball for treatment planning.
plos-pone-0004151: In 2009, Hu, Metselaar, and Ben calmed brain autoimmunity with tiny drug carriers. PEG-coated minocycline liposomes eased central nervous system autoimmune disease in mice. The drug-loaded bubbles delivered therapy past the blood-brain barrier. The clever carrier design boosts minocycline's reach greatly.
plos-pone-0004251: In 2009, a British team read leukemia's chemical diary closely. Chemical scans tracked drug responses in acute myeloid leukaemia cell lines closely. Bezafibrate plus a progestin shifted the cells' chemistry quite fast in dishes. The metabolic map guides smart drug reuse efforts today.
plos-pone-0004351: In 2009, Klarkowski, Wazome, and Lokuge fixed HIV testing in eastern Congo. A rapid in-situ HIV confirmation test was tested in a struggling high-failure program. False positives had long plagued the program. The quick test could restore trust in results fast.
plos-pone-0358051: Anxiety and withdrawal in middle childhood often go untreated until they harden. This study tested inhibitory control training — exercises in stopping automatic responses — as a universal prevention strategy for internalizing complaints. The results show whether a simple cognitive workout can protect young minds before problems take root.
plos-pone-0358951: Training preschool teachers to observe children well is harder than it sounds. This design-based study combined virtual simulation with real classroom video to build observational skills in teacher candidates. The sequential program shows how digital practice plus authentic footage sharpens a teacher’s eye before they enter a real classroom.
plos-pone-0358451: Breeding better crops means predicting which seedlings will yield most — years before harvest. This paper built a parallel convolution attention network that reads crop genomes and predicts performance. The deep-learning model gives breeders a faster way to pick winners from DNA alone.
plos-pone-0357951: Guava and Mexican sunflower — combined as an aqueous extract — may steady metabolism and protect the gut. This paper showed the plant duo improves metabolic homeostasis and preserves intestinal integrity in preclinical models. The combination emerges as a natural candidate for metabolic therapy worth testing further.
plos-pone-0355051: Linking medical records to insurance claims without exposing patient identities is a delicate balancing act. This paper evaluated the completeness of a tokenized medical record dataset for hemophilia B linked to administrative claims. The evaluation validates privacy-preserving research methods that protect patients while enabling science.
plos-pone-0357051: Grouting materials made from mixed solid waste need reliable strength predictions before anyone pours them. This paper built a prediction model for the compressive strength of alkali-activated multi-source solid-waste grouting materials using generative adversarial networks and machine learning. The AI forecasts strength directly from the mix design.
plos-pone-0357451: A full-thickness macular hole threatens central vision — and surgery is the only fix. This Tanzanian hospital study reported the visual and anatomical outcomes of macular hole surgery along with associated factors. The outcomes show what skilled surgery can achieve for patients in this setting.
plos-pone-0354251: Saudi Arabia’s historic driving reform — letting women drive — rippled through workplaces. This ordered logit analysis studied women’s workplace transitions following the reform. The transitions quantify, in hard data, how mobility translated into economic participation.
plos-pone-0356551: Midwifery and nursing educators in Ethiopia need modern assessment methods. This 2023 study examined the implementation of objective structured clinical examinations among educators at South and Central Region universities. The findings show what it takes to bring rigorous clinical testing to resource-constrained training.
plos-pone-0355551: Oxfendazole could be a game-changer against liver flukes — if it can reach them. This paper investigated the pharmacokinetic barriers to the drug’s flukicidal efficacy. Understanding where the drug fails to penetrate points reformulators toward versions that actually kill the parasites.
plos-pone-0352551: Building on saline soils — where salt corrodes foundations — demands specialized engineering. This experimental study examined the vertical load-bearing performance of single piles and pile groups in saline soil foundations. The load test data tell engineers how deep and how many piles salt-country structures truly need.
plos-pone-0354151: Leatherback sea turtles cross entire oceans — and their genes record the journeys. This paper presented a worldwide phylogeography of Dermochelys coriacea, covering evolution, conservation, and nomenclature standardization through haplotype analysis. The global genetic map guides protection of Earth’s largest turtle across all its ocean basins.
plos-pone-0355951: Nursing students’ attitudes toward palliative care shape the deaths they’ll attend. This cross-sectional study examined the factors associated with those attitudes — including students’ personal experiences with loss. The findings show that lived experience, not just lectures, builds the compassion dying patients need.
plos-pone-0354751: Targeting liver disease genes with siRNA — without animal testing — is now possible. This paper showed a chemically optimized, GalNAc-conjugated siRNA targeting HSD17B13 works in a human 3D organoid model of MASH liver disease. The organoid-validated therapy offers a cruelty-free path to treating fatty liver disease.
plos-pone-0355851: Rocks creep — deforming slowly under sustained load — and their creep parameters degrade over time. This paper built a viscoelastic-plastic creep model based on that degradation. The model helps engineers predict the slow-motion failures of tunnels, mines, and slopes.
plos-pone-0354351: Buzzer iron cores — tiny but essential — need automated defect detection. This paper developed a machine vision-based detection method for them. The automated inspection catches flaws invisible to the rushing human eye — improving the reliability of countless electronic devices.
europmc-pmc2813751: Chemotherapy is usually seen as suppressing immunity, but this 2010 paper argues the opposite can happen. The authors show that pre-treatment with chemotherapy can make tumors more visible to the immune system, boosting adaptive immune responses against them. The finding supports combining chemo with immunotherapy. It reframed an old drug class as a possible immune ally.
europmc-pmc2876151: Cell division runs on a master switch called Cdk1. This 2010 review surveys the targets and processes under Cdk1 control, from DNA copying to cell splitting. The authors' overview maps the switch's vast reach. The review is a handy reference for the cell cycle's command center.
europmc-pmc2893951: Animal research reports were often too thin to trust. This 2010 paper delivers the ARRIVE guidelines for reporting animal research in full. The authors' checklist demands the details science needs to judge and repeat work. Their standards, widely adopted, lifted the field's openness.
europmc-pmc2910551: Fat tissue talks to the immune system, and the conversation can turn hostile. This 2010 review covers the role of adipose tissue and adipokines in obesity-linked inflammatory diseases. The authors' overview connects fat signals to illness. Their synthesis explains why obesity inflames.
europmc-pmc2920551: The shellfish poison saxitoxin has kin. This 2010 review covers nerve-harming alkaloids, saxitoxin and its look-alikes. The authors chart the clan's makeup. Their guide aids spotting tainted seafood. It pulls together chemistry, biology, and detection in one place. Shellfish farmers and food-safety labs both use it as a reference.
europmc-pmc2923151: Brains in conversation may sync up. This 2010 paper reports inter-brain synchronization during social interaction. The authors' dual recordings reveal coupled rhythms between partners. Their finding opened a window on the social brain. Later work used the same trick to study teamwork and empathy.
europmc-pmc2930851: White blood cells live fast and die young, and this 2010 review tracks them. The authors cover neutrophil kinetics in health and disease. Their overview follows the short, violent life of a front-line defender. The review aids reading immune counts.
europmc-pmc2973851: Sorting structured gene pools needs sharp math. This 2010 paper brings a new way to tell apart mixed groups from DNA data. The authors' method became a go-to for gene-pool studies. The work spread far and wide. Wildlife teams use it to track herds and schools.
europmc-pmc2976751: Rebuilding species trees from gene trees takes the right math. This 2010 paper offers a maximum pseudo-likelihood approach for estimating species trees under the coalescent model. The authors' fast method scales up. Their work aided big phylogenies. Thousands of species now slot into place.
europmc-pmc2990751: Tumor sorting can work from a single sample. This 2010 paper brings a simple template-matching method for sorting tumors with confidence scores. The author's method eases diagnosis. Their tool aided cancer typing. Clinics type tumors without big reference sets. The code is free for clinics to use.
europmc-pmc3004851: Smoking scrambles the airway's germs. This 2010 paper finds jumbled germ communities in smokers' upper airways. The authors' gene sequencing reveals the chaos. Their work links smoke to airway disease. Quitters' airways slowly regain healthy germs. The chaos may seed chronic lung infections.
europmc-pmc3069751: Crystal structures got a refiner. This 2011 paper covers REFMAC5, the workhorse for polishing crystal structures. The authors' program became a lab standard. Their software shaped structural biology. Every deposited structure likely passed through it. The refiner squeezes signal from noise.
europmc-pmc3082551: Aging rats run low on NAD+ and Sirt1. This 2011 paper tracks falling NAD+, rising oxidant stress, and fading Sirt1 in aging rats. The authors chart the decline. Their work backs NAD+ boosters. Old organs showed the steepest drops. Supplement sellers cite the study widely.
europmc-pmc3094351: A lifetime of inflammation shortens chromosome caps. This 2011 study ties piled-up inflammation to shorter telomeres in older adults. The authors bridge inflammation and aging. Their work backs anti-inflammatory living. Exercise and sleep slowed the shortening. The effect rivaled smoking's toll.
europmc-pmc6506551: Some materials keep glowing briefly after the lights go out, a trick called room-temperature phosphorescence. It used to need metal-based compounds, but chemists have now coaxed it out of purely carbon-based organic molecules instead. This review explains how careful molecule design boosts their glow, pointing toward cheaper and safer materials for displays, sensors, and bio-imaging.
europmc-pmc6509751: When Pseudomonas aeruginosa grows as a biofilm - a slimy, surface-clinging community - antibiotics that kill free-floating cells often fail against it. This review gathers how these films slow drug entry, shelter sleeper cells, and switch on resistance genes, letting a top hospital threat slip past treatment. It also maps strategies that might crack the biofilm and give old antibiotics a second chance.
europmc-pmc6579551: Rheumatoid arthritis varies wildly - and a peek inside the joint may predict who responds to standard drugs. Analyzing synovial tissue from 144 untreated patients, researchers linked cellular and molecular signatures to treatment outcomes. The tissue fingerprints forecast who benefits from conventional DMARDs and whose joint damage will march on.
europmc-pmc6594651: Finding which drug grabs which protein target is slow bench work - so computers are learning to guess. DeepConv-DTI feeds protein sequences into a deep-learning network that predicts drug-target pairings. The model spots promising matches far faster than lab assays, narrowing the hunt for new medicines.
europmc-pmc6628851: What counts as a healthy diet differs by country - this review compares them all. Surveying food-based dietary guidelines worldwide, the authors map where nations agree (vegetables, whole grains) and where they part ways. The global snapshot helps policymakers borrow what works and spot gaps in their own advice.
europmc-pmc6683051: The trillions of microbes in the gut shape far more than digestion - weight, immunity, even mood. This sweeping review connects the gut microbiome to diet and chronic disease, from metabolic disorders to bowel cancer. Feeding the right microbes may be among the cheapest medicines.
europmc-pmc6711451: Brain scans show regions talking - but who influences whom? This tutorial's second part walks through group-level analysis with Parametric Empirical Bayes: how to test whether connection strengths differ across people. Worked examples make the heavy statistics of effective connectivity approachable.
europmc-pmc6723551: The immune system runs on food - every defender cell needs fuel. This review maps how diet shapes immune function: which nutrients arm the defenses and what happens when they run short. Eating well, the evidence says, is genuinely a form of immune maintenance.
europmc-pmc6767151: A popular stats transformation promised tidy meta-analyses - and quietly lied. This paper shows the inverse Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation can produce seriously misleading results when combining proportions. The cautionary tale: fancy math needs checking, not trust.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-51: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report reviews NASA's Ares I rocket — the planned crew launcher for the post-shuttle era. GAO found the agency had taken steps toward sound investment decisions but still faced major gaps in what it knew about cost, schedule, and technical risk. The report reads as an early warning about a program that would later be canceled amid exactly the problems GAO flagged.
gao-gaoreports-b-309751: The Borenstein Group challenged a federal communications contract in 2007, and GAO's ruling settles it. The marketing shop said the award was unfair; the call measures the claim against bid law. In the niche market for government ad and media work, the ruling marks where the creative pitch meets the legal rulebook.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-851: The Pentagon's personnel overhaul was flying without instruments in 2007 — GAO's report says it needed better controls and cost visibility. The findings target the management fog around the new HR system. The report demands a dashboard for one of the largest workforce experiments ever tried.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-651: Katrina's poison lingered in 2007 — GAO's report says the EPA's environmental work on the Gulf could do more by facing its information gaps. The findings press the agency to fill the data holes. The report argues that cleanup without good maps is just expensive guessing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-351: The bank insurer's cyber program needed staying power in 2007 — GAO's report says the FDIC had to keep up its security gains. The findings press for persistence, not one-time fixes. The report's message: the deposit guardian's own vault must stay locked tight.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-451: The Pentagon's back-office blueprint was getting a redesign in 2007 — GAO's report lays out the plan for shaping the business systems map. The findings sketch the new concept in plain terms. The report's hope: draw the firm's nervous system before you start rewiring it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-151: Small firms loved the Pentagon's mentoring program in 2007, and GAO's report says the proteges valued the help, though the yearly reports to Congress needed work. The findings praise the program and prod the paperwork. The mentorship was real; the metrics were not.
openalex-w7204452651: Legal language can lock ordinary people out of justice. This article studies how the wording used in Brazil's small-claims courts blocks access, and proposes plain, inclusive communication, including audio options, for people in vulnerable situations. The authors argue that being understood is a right, not a courtesy. A justice-reform paper where clarity itself is the remedy.
openalex-w7160540551: Squeezed under pressure, an organic crystal hovers at a quantum tipping point. This experimental paper studies weak antilocalization, a quantum interference effect, in a Dirac semimetal driven toward an insulating state. The authors measured how electron coherence fades with temperature. A precision study of quantum matter at the edge of change.
openalex-w4417098251: Superconductors and magnets are usually rivals, but this theory paper finds a hidden kinship. The authors show that the math for an exotic superconductor can be reshaped into the math for magnetism with spin-orbit coupling, a twist linking electron spin to motion. A bridge between two quantum phenomena, built with pen-and-paper theory.
openalex-w7154973251: Shake a box of grains and the flow turns strange. This physics paper studies a gas of hard grains under shear, showing its viscosity jumps suddenly as the shear rate changes. The authors derive the S-shaped response from kinetic theory. A granular-physics study of sand behaving like no ordinary fluid.
openalex-w7155093551: Killing stomach germs sounds easy, but drug resistance fights back. This study tracked ten years of H. pylori cure rates at a regional hospital, watching first- and second-round treatments. The team tied results to resistance trends. A gut-medicine study of a moving target.
openalex-w7211866551: After a brain bleed, surgeons may remove part of the skull to relieve pressure. This retrospective study hunted predictors of who needs that drastic step after acute subdural hematoma. The authors analyzed postoperative swelling factors. A neurosurgery study of when to open the skull.
pmc-13470151: This 2026 pediatric oncology paper works toward a clear definition of cachexia — severe wasting of muscle and weight — in children with cancer in the United States. Without a shared definition, doctors can't measure or treat it consistently. The framework the authors build is a first step toward better care for these young patients.
pmc-13474951: In this 2026 materials chemistry paper, researchers tuned the flexibility and porosity of MIL-53(Sc)-fum — a metal-organic framework, a crystal with molecule-sized pores — by swapping its cluster anions. They isolated conformational isomers using solvent changes. Fine control over pore breathing matters for gas storage and separation applications.
pmc-13464051: In this 2026 immunology study, mice whose immune response depends on T cells were infected with Leishmania amazonensis, a parasite that causes skin and tissue disease. The work examines how T-cell-driven immunity affects the survival and virulence of the parasite's amastigote stage. Findings feed into vaccine and treatment design for leishmaniasis.
pmc-13571351: This 2026 cardiology case report describes transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair performed under argatroban — a heparin alternative — in a patient on heart-lung support with suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Every element raised the stakes. The successful case shows the procedure is feasible even in extreme circumstances.
pmc-13549951: This 2026 cancer paper describes creating prostate-specific, SKP2-humanized mice via CRISPR knock-in — mice carrying the human version of the SKP2 gene in the prostate. The model revealed how neoplastic initiation and microenvironmental reprogramming unfold. Humanized models like this bridge the gap to human prostate cancer.
pmc-13449251: A 2026 evolutionary biology paper showing that NOD-like receptor genes — immune sensors — undergo diversity-enhancing evolution in a fungal species complex. Fungi need immune-like recognition too, and the genes are under strong selection. The study extends immunity's evolutionary story beyond animals and plants.
pmc-13463551: This 2026 chemistry paper describes a PET-trackable, carborane-conjugated star-shaped poly(2-oxazoline) scaffold carrying a high boron payload with improved water solubility — designed for boron neutron capture therapy, per the truncated title. Getting enough boron into tumors is the therapy's bottleneck. The scaffold is engineered to solve it.
pmc-13341951: A 2026 study linking testosterone levels to lean soft tissue and handgrip strength in middle-aged men. The hormone-body composition connection is well known but the details matter for healthy aging. The findings inform how testosterone is interpreted clinically.
pmc-13439951: A 2026 crop genetics paper measuring the change in deleterious mutation burden of barley germplasm conserved over one regeneration cycle. Seed banks must regenerate stocks without accumulating harmful mutations. The measurement validates conservation practice.
pmc-13422751: A 2026 case report of radiographic enhancing progression without molecular or histologic progression in IDH-mutant grade 2 astrocytoma treated with an IDH inhibitor. The scan lied; the tumor hadn't grown. The case warns against over-reading imaging.
pmc-13425951: In this 2026 prospective cohort study, self-efficacy and sense of coherence affected hand disability during the first year after distal radius fracture surgery. Mindset shaped recovery. The cohort data quantify the psychological contribution.
pmc-13530651: A 2026 conference paper arguing pitch count alone isn't enough — age-dependent pinch strength changes and associated factors in youth baseball pitchers. The young arms needed more metrics. The paper makes the case.
pmc-13529151: This 2026 oncology paper associated thymidine kinase 1 with clinicopathological high-risk features in breast cancer. The proliferation marker flagged aggressive disease. The association supports its use.
pmc-13502851: A 2026 bibliometric paper on global research trends of digital applications in medical education. The field's growth was mapped. The trends guide educators.
pmc-13478251: In this 2026 real-world study, outcomes of acute myeloid leukemia patients on FLT3, IDH1, or IDH2-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy were reported. The targeted drugs' real-world performance was measured. The outcomes inform practice.
pmc-13473751: This 2026 paper tested feasibility and safety of washed microbiota transplantation as salvage therapy for refractory non-CDI gut pathogens in critically ill patients. The desperate intervention was evaluated. The feasibility data are preliminary.
pmc-13469751: This 2026 systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression examined age and treatment efficacy in myasthenia gravis. The age-treatment interaction was quantified. The analysis guides therapy across ages.
pmc-13457351: A 2026 neuroimaging paper on brain morphometry patterns in the presence of Alzheimer's disease and/or LATE neuropathologic changes. The two pathologies' structural signatures were compared. The patterns aid diagnosis.
pmc-13454951: This 2026 systems pharmacology model of aging identified optimal combination therapies with secondary benefits on weight loss and metabolic health. The aging model optimized drug combos. The secondary benefits are the bonus.
pmc-13439351: A 2026 transplant paper comparing early graft dysfunction scores in liver transplantation after ex-situ normothermic machine perfusion. The perfusion-era scores were evaluated. The comparison guides assessment.
pmc-13428351: A 2026 epilepsy paper on astrocyte subtype-specific alterations in the dentate gyrus of individuals with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. The glial subtypes changed specifically. The alterations are the pathology detail.
pmc-13495551: This 2026 chemistry paper took an organometallic chemistry approach to peptide tricycles. The metal-mediated macrocyclization is the innovation. The tricycles are the products.
pmc-13500351: A 2026 English cross-sectional survey of healthcare professionals on non-cigarette tobacco cessation support — current provision, confidence, and barriers (the title is truncated). The cessation support gaps were identified. The barriers guide training.
pmc-13466951: A 2026 double-blind RCT: bisphenol A decreased peripheral insulin sensitivity in normal-weight adults. The plastic chemical's metabolic harm was proven experimentally. The decrease is the warning.
pmc-13452151: In this 2026 systematic review, drug stock-outs in HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria programs were examined. The supply chain failures were documented. The review demands action.
pmc-13440051: This 2026 first-principles study examined tetragonal distortion of the multiferroic compound alpha-LiFe5O8. The quantum calculations revealed the distortion. The study is the materials physics.
pmc-13513151: A 2026 historical review of biomarkers of cardiovascular stress. The heart stress markers' history was traced. The review is the reference.
pmc-13486851: In this 2026 study, non-fatal firearm violence was tracked across 17 US cities using police dashboard data from 2020 to 2025. The shootings' patterns were mapped. The tracking is the public health surveillance.
pmc-13462051: In this 2026 Japanese psychometric paper, a comprehensive scale for measuring explanatory models of mental disorders was developed. The cultural beliefs about mental illness were quantified. The scale serves cross-cultural psychiatry.
pmc-13634051: A 2026 genetics paper: PALM3 and hearing loss — a potential dual diagnosis interfering with novel gene discovery. The confounding diagnosis was flagged. The paper warns gene hunters.
pmc-13418051: In this 2026 colorectal cancer paper, UFL1-mediated UFMylation of ENO1 restrained aerobic glycolysis and cancer progression. The protein modification braked the Warburg effect. The restraining is the therapeutic target.
arxiv-2606-15951: Physicists created an exotic state of matter — a fractional quantum Hall fluid — by gently moving atoms out of a Bose-Einstein condensate, the coldest state of matter known. The process was slow and careful ("adiabatic") so the delicate quantum properties survived. The paper reports the experiment and what it demonstrates about building quantum matter atom by atom.
arxiv-2606-16151: AI models that "show their work" can still invent reasoning steps that don't follow from the context. GRACE is a benchmark that checks faithfulness step by step: does each individual step really follow from what the model was given? It is a test suite for researchers who want AI reasoning they can actually trust, not just fluent-sounding chains of thought.
arxiv-2606-16351: Talk tech sings best on mixed voices, yet transmasc tones are scant in the packs. TMASC is a first big voice chest of transmasc speech, fit for voice study and for how folks feel about their own tone. It aids talk-tech crews who want all voices heard.
arxiv-2606-16651: Social media is often blamed for harming teens, but design choices matter enormously. This paper maps the design space for youth social media around a different center: building real friendships. The framework gives designers and policymakers a friendship-first lens for evaluating and creating platforms for young people.
